newsitem.title: INDIA: India's RBI to propose plan for exporters - minister.
newsitem.headline: India's RBI to propose plan for exporters - minister.

text.p: Indian Commerce Minister Bolla Buli Ramaiah said on Friday that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) would soon propose a plan to help exporters.
"They will come out with a proposal that will enable to help further the export-oriented industry," Ramaiah told Reuters.
Ramaiah said the government was in discussions with the central bank about exporters' complaints over a perceived liquidity crunch.
He said the RBI was working on "some schemes" which "will be able to come out very soon, most probably within a few days". He did not elaborate.
On Thursday, the Commerce Ministry announced a slowdown in export growth in August which analysts called worrisome.
Exports were valued at $2.60 billion in August, 2.38 percent higher than in the same month in 1995.
In August 1995, exports were 20.66 percent higher than in the same month in 1994.

V. Raghuraman, secretary general of the Associated Chambers of Commerce (ASSOCHAM), said on Thursday that the slowdown in export growth was "worrisome and strengthens fears of an overall economic slowdown".
